description:
FILED s473t6b (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 round 9.

PERL: `${^LAST_FH}` is a read-only GLOB REFERENCE to the handle most recently
read from or written to -- set by `readline`, `print`, `tell`, `eof`, `seek`
and friends.  For a bareword handle it is a ref to that glob; for a lexical
handle it is a ref to the SCALAR holding the glob ("referencing lexical
coercible glob").

PCL: `${^LAST_FH}` is undef, always; nothing sets it.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL, probes/p3.pl H2):

    open my $fh, '<', 'p3.pl' or die;
    my $t = tell $fh;
    printf "lastfh=%s isref=%s\n",
      (defined ${^LAST_FH} ? 'def' : 'undef'), (ref(${^LAST_FH}) || '(none)');

    perl: lastfh=def isref=GLOB
    PCL:  lastfh=undef isref=(none)

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/magic.t 159 `${^LAST_FH} after tell`,
160 `${^LAST_FH} after another tell`, 161 `${^LAST_FH} referencing lexical
coercible glob`.

SHAPE: one place to write it -- the handle resolution every IO op already goes
through (`%p-out-target` for the write side, the readline/tell/eof side's own
resolver) -- plus a read-only magic cell for the name.  The cost is one store
per IO op, which is why it wants to be set where the handle object is already
in hand rather than in each op.  The `ref` answer has to be a GLOB ref for a
bareword and a SCALAR ref for a lexical handle, which is #1664's typeglob
model; the two rows that ask for the bareword spelling are behind it.

Low value on its own (3 rows) -- a filler, or free once #1664 lands.
subject: ${^LAST_FH} is undef in PCL -- nothing sets it; perl makes it a glob ref to the handle most recently read from or written to (3 op/magic.t rows)
